info.name: llama
info.description:
llama.cpp `llama-server` endpoints — GGUF-quantized models exposed via an OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface plus llama.cpp-native extras. Every service in `ai/llama/docker-compose.llama.yml` is a standalone llama-server; the default deploy publishes the `glm5.2` container on `localhost:8010` (see `PORT_LLAMA_GLM52` in `.env`) with model alias `glm5.2`. The other two services are `qwen3.8-flash` on `localhost:8017` (`PORT_LLAMA_QWEN38_FLASH`, variable `llamaQwen38Flash`) and `glm5.3-flash` on `localhost:8020` (`PORT_LLAMA_GLM53_FLASH`, variable `llamaGlm53Flash`) — the latter is the CPU + RAM-only GLM-5.3-Flash service with no GPU, so budget minutes for time-to-first-token on large prompts. The fourth, `qwen3.5-4b` on `localhost:8028` (`PORT_LLAMA_QWEN35_4B`, variable `llamaQwen35_4b`, folder 'qwen3.5-4b'), is a small CPU-only model that only the document classifier's model registry calls (route-policy's `llm_classifier` evaluator) — it is not in LiteLLM. Set the collection variable `llama` to the direct-port base URL (default http://localhost:8010) — no auth is required on the direct port per LLAMA.md.

The 'Via LiteLLM' folder routes chat through the unified LiteLLM proxy at `{{litellm}}/v1/chat/completions` using the same `glm5.2` alias (registered in `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml` → `model_list`). LiteLLM requires bearer auth via a virtual master key.

Notes:
- `/v1/embeddings` is only mounted when `llama-server` is launched with `--embedding` (or `--pooling`). The current `glm5.2` command in `docker-compose.llama.yml` does NOT enable it, so no embeddings request is included by default. Add `--embedding` to the service `command:` block and uncomment the equivalent request if you need it.
- First request after container start is slow — llama.cpp runs a warmup pass on the first inference call (see LLAMA.md § Non-obvious constraints).
- The healthcheck has a 900 s `start_period` to cover the initial GGUF download; `/health` will 503 while the model is still loading.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `llama.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents the fields this stack uses of each request and response body: an open subset of the upstream API. Errors answer the server's own OpenAI-style error object and are not repeated per endpoint.

variable.description: Direct-port base URL for the `glm5.2` llama-server container. Published on `${PORT_LLAMA_GLM52}` (default 8010) → container port 8000. On `ai_shared` it's http://glm5.2:8000. LLAMA.md § Quick start. No auth required — the port is meant to sit behind LiteLLM.

Model alias returned by `/v1/models` and required in the `"model"` field of chat/completion requests. Set via `-a glm5.2` in the compose `command:` block. If you add more llama-server services (see LLAMA.md § Adding more models), each one carries its own alias.

Direct-port base URL for the `qwen3.8-flash` llama-server container. Published on `${PORT_LLAMA_QWEN38_FLASH}` (default 8017) → container port 8000. On `ai_shared` it's http://qwen3.8-flash:8000. Model alias is `qwen3.8-flash`. Launched with the thinking-mode sampling defaults from the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model card (LLAMA.md § `qwen3.8-flash` sampling defaults).

Direct-port base URL for the `glm5.3-flash` llama-server container. Published on `${PORT_LLAMA_GLM53_FLASH}` (default 8020) → container port 8000. On `ai_shared` it's http://glm5.3-flash:8000. Model alias is `glm5.3-flash`. This service runs GLM-5.3-Flash entirely on CPU + system RAM (no GPU) with MTP speculative decoding, so expect a long time-to-first-token on big prompts (LLAMA.md § `glm5.3-flash` — GLM-5.3-Flash on CPU and RAM only).

Direct-port base URL for the `qwen3.5-4b` llama-server container (folder 'qwen3.5-4b'). Published on `${PORT_LLAMA_QWEN35_4B}` (default 8028) → container port 8000. On `ai_shared` it's http://qwen3.5-4b:8000 — the URL of the `qwen3.5-4b` entry in `ai/classifier/models.yaml`. Model alias is `qwen3.5-4b`. CPU only, thinking off by default, not registered in LiteLLM (LLAMA.md § `qwen3.5-4b` — a small CPU model for route-policy).
LiteLLM base URL for the 'Via LiteLLM' folder. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the `glm5.2` model. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` only by requests inside the 'Via LiteLLM' folder — direct-port requests need no auth.

request.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completion against the `qwen3.8-flash` llama-server container (port 8017 by default). The service is launched with thinking-mode sampling defaults (`--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --presence-penalty 0.0`) baked into the compose `command:` block — see LLAMA.md § `qwen3.8-flash` sampling defaults. Override any of those per-request by passing `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, or `presence_penalty` in the JSON body. Add `"stream": true` for SSE streaming.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

OpenAI-compatible chat completion against the `glm5.3-flash` llama-server container (port 8020 by default) — GLM-5.3-Flash running entirely on CPU + RAM with MTP speculative decoding. Server defaults baked into the compose `command:` block: `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95`, chat-template `reasoning_effort=low`, `--reasoning-budget 8192`, `--n-predict 32768`. Override sampling per request via `temperature` / `top_p`; override the thinking level with `chat_template_kwargs: {"reasoning_effort": "low" | "high" | "max"}` (anything else is treated as `max`). Streaming (`"stream": true`) is strongly recommended — on a long uncached prompt the first token can take minutes because prompt processing runs on CPU. Errors: 503 while the model is still downloading / mlocking (first start: ~148 GB). LLAMA.md § `glm5.3-flash` — GLM-5.3-Flash on CPU and RAM only.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

OpenAI-compatible chat completion with Server-Sent Events. Response is a stream of `data: {...}` chunks terminated by `data: [DONE]`, each chunk containing a `choices[0].delta.content` fragment. Postman shows the raw event stream in the response body.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: qwen3.5-4b
item.description: The `qwen3.5-4b` llama-server container at `{{llamaQwen35_4b}}` (default http://localhost:8028, no auth): Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M on CPU only, the model route-policy's `llm_classifier` evaluator scores conversation transcripts with through the document classifier's `POST /assess` (`model: qwen3.5-4b`). Not registered in LiteLLM, so there is no 'Via LiteLLM' request for it. The requests here are the box checks of LLAMA.md § `qwen3.5-4b` — a small CPU model for route-policy.

request.description:
Liveness probe for `qwen3.5-4b`. Returns `{"status":"ok"}` once the 2.74 GB Q4_K_M GGUF has downloaded and loaded; 503 while it is still loading (the healthcheck's `start_period` is 600 s for the first download). LLAMA.md § `qwen3.5-4b` — a small CPU model for route-policy.

#### Schemas

See *GET /health*, the first request of this endpoint.

OpenAI-compatible chat completion shaped like a classifier scoring call: `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}` (llama-server turns it into a JSON grammar) and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` — the same kwarg the classifier's `qwen3.5-4b` registry entry sends in its `extra_body`, and the server's own default (`--chat-template-kwargs`). Expect `choices[0].message.content` to be the JSON alone, with no `<think>` block and no `reasoning_content`, in a few dozen completion tokens; `timings` (llama.cpp's addition to the response) shows prompt and generation speed on CPU. Server defaults: `--temp 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --presence-penalty 0.0` (the model card's instruct preset without its presence penalty), `--n-predict 512` caps `max_tokens`. 503 while the model is loading. LLAMA.md § `qwen3.5-4b` — a small CPU model for route-policy.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: Via LiteLLM
item.description: Chat routed through the unified LiteLLM proxy at `{{litellm}}` instead of hitting the llama-server port directly. LiteLLM's `model_list` entry for `glm5.2` (see `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml`) forwards to `http://glm5.2:8000/v1` over the `ai_shared` Docker network. Requires bearer auth via a virtual master key — set the `virtual master key` collection variable. Use this path when you want unified logging / rate-limiting / retries / spend tracking across all backends.

request.description:
Same OpenAI-compatible chat surface as the direct-port `/v1/chat/completions`, but proxied through LiteLLM. The `"model"` field must be `glm5.2` — that's the `model_name` LiteLLM matches on to route to the `openai/glm5.2` provider block. LiteLLM strips its virtual key and forwards to llama-server with `api_key: none`. Response shape is identical to the direct call. LLAMA.md § LiteLLM integration.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Streaming chat via LiteLLM. Same SSE `data: {...}` / `data: [DONE]` shape as the direct-port streaming request; LiteLLM passes chunks through as they arrive from llama-server. Look at LiteLLM logs (`make logs litellm`) if the stream stalls — the `stream_timeout` in `litellm_config.yaml` caps how long the proxy waits between chunks.

#### Schemas

See *POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.
